I also re-derived the plate baselines with the SAME Lanczos scale-match I used in r8 and they reproduce to the digit: plate-01 @1280x720 median_area_px 24.0 / area_p95_over_median 8.36 / pct_iou_ge_090 23.12, plate-01 @640x360 23.0 / 5.51 / 19.09. So the r8->r9 deltas below are real and not an artefact of a changed method or a refit mask. I hand-rolled nothing.
biggestGap: The distribution SHAPE has landed but the POPULATION has not: the hero carries 66 resolvable droplets against plate-01's 333 at the same 1280x720 raster and the frame lost more than half its juice this round (droplets mask_px 24884 -> 6507), because r9 reshaped a fixed ~60-object emitter budget (q.rim 120 / q.spray 210, both untouched) downward in size instead of adding the sub-resolution grain population that makes plate-02 a dense continuum -- and since every size law is WORLD-space, the whole reshape falls under the sub-pixel floor in portrait, where 04-cut+250ms area_p95_over_median went 1.86 -> 1.90 against landscape's 2.66 -> 5.14.

1_THE_BIGGEST_GAP_MEASURED_THE_COUNT_NEV.the_instrument_warning_I_am_obliged_to_r: area_p95_over_median is a RATIO, and on the hero it improved 6.37 -> 8.66 while BOTH of its terms fell -- median 74.5 -> 40.0 and p95 475 -> 346. The plate is median 24.0 / p95 201. So we now match the plate's ratio at ~1.7x the plate's absolute scale in both terms. A metric that can be satisfied by scaling the whole population down is one that can eventually be satisfied by deleting it; this is the same failure mode as the denominator finding earlier in this project. It has NOT been gamed here -- median_area_px is quoted alongside and moved the right way toward an absolute target -- but the next round must not chase p95/median without an absolute floor on mask_px, and no future acceptance gate should cite the ratio alone.
1_THE_BIGGEST_GAP_MEASURED_THE_COUNT_NEV.what_it_looks_like: shots/r9/00-hero.png at 1:1: ~66 discrete red lozenges and a dozen white specks, separated by large fields of pure black. plate-02 at the same magnification is a CONTINUUM -- thousands of grains packed densely enough that the cloud has an internal texture and a soft outer boundary, with no readable gaps. That difference, not the size of any one drop, is what makes the blind call take under a second. It fails in motion as well as in a still, which by the calibration is exactly what sits between 74 and 81.
1_THE_BIGGEST_GAP_MEASURED_THE_COUNT_NEV.why_it_is_cheap_to_fix: The drop pool is NDROP = maxBeads 9000 (fluid.js:415) and a burst currently emits rim 120 + spray 210 + mist <=1500, so there are thousands of free slots. Drops are ONE instanced draw. Raising the count costs no draw calls and no programs -- the landscape budget has room (111 calls against 120).

evidence.BLIND_TEST: Handed the two unlabelled, I pick ours in about a second, and it is still the POPULATION that does it, not any single drop. An r9 drop cropped at 8x I would genuinely hesitate on -- the optical interior from r8 survives, the sizes are now varied, the fast-flick aerosol frame is close enough to plate-02's morphology that I would have to look at the fruit rather than the juice to call it. But the whole frame is ~66 separated objects on black with readable gaps between them, and plate-02 is a packed continuum with internal texture and a soft outer boundary. Add the two comb/zipper objects in the hero, which no real spray contains, and the call is immediate. The gap between 74 and 81 is a count, not a shader.
